messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH alert fired — metric=inference_gateway.5xx_rate, env=prod, window=5m, value=18.3% (>10%). Pager escalation path: oncall -> secondary -> englead. See PD: https://pd.example/INC12345
Tina (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Can someone grab quick blast of customer-impact?
Ashley (support): getting customer DMs that API calls 502 intermittently since ~4m ago. No outage page on status yet but several reports.
Jon SRE: checking dashboards… tailing logs now. Looks like 502s originating from ingress -> routing layer, spike in upstream 503/504 from kvcache pods.
Jon SRE: running quick query: `sum(increase(http_requests_total{code=~\"5..\",service=\"inference-gateway\",env=\"prod\"}[5m])) by (code)` returns a bunch of 502 and 504. Also seeing elevated p50 latency.
Tina (oncall): are there any recent deploys?
Kevin (englead): I rolled a small canary for model-routing 20m ago, but no mass rollout. I'll check the canary subset. If it's inflicting routing rules we may rollback.
Luca (platform): I see autoscaler spikes on routing-proxy in us-west1 at 09:14UTC. Some pods are reporting `ReadTimeout` to the backend pool. Possible backend starvation.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation sent to Kevin (englead). PD link: https://pd.example/INC12345/esc
Kevin (englead): I'm jumping in. Jon, can you capture the latest `kubectl describe` of one failing proxy pod and paste errors?
Jon SRE: paste logs snippet:
```
[09:13:54] proxy-7f9b8 ReadTimeout backend=kvcache-3 target=10.42.3.12:8080
[09:13:55] proxy-7f9b8 502 UpstreamError: connection reset by peer
[09:14:01] proxy-7f9b8 504 BackendTimeout: downstream queue full
```
Jon SRE: Also high socket backlog on that node. Kernel dmesg shows `accept: too many open files` on kvcache pods.
Tina (oncall): Could this be a networking flake in the AZ? Are multiple AZs affected?
Luca (platform): At least 3 nodes in us-west1-b show similar networking drops. Other regions (eu-west1) normal. Looks region-scoped.
Kevin (englead): mitigation plan: 1) scale routing-proxy pool + add transient capacity in us-west1, 2) divert traffic away from affected subset via weight change, 3) if canary implicated -> rollback canary. Jon, initiate scale and reroute. Tina, keep customers updated.
Jon SRE: scaling proxy pool now: `k scale --replicas=40 deployment/routing-proxy-usw1` -> started. Also adjusting route weights to divert 30% traffic to eu-west fallback for non-latency-sensitive customers.
Jon SRE: scaling reported success. New pods coming up and passing readiness.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Auto-rotation: new proxy pods joined LB. Health checks passing.
Ashley (support): Posted a short status to customers: "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors in US-West; teams are actively mitigating. We will update in 15 minutes." Link: https://status.example/incidents/INC12345
Tina (oncall): Jon, any sign canary rollback needed?
Jon SRE: canary still at 5% but trending like rest of traffic — not unique. I won't rollback yet. More likely node-level network issues hitting kvcache. Rolling restarts on kvcache might help but careful about cache-warm penalty.
Kevin (englead): Do controlled restarts on unhealthy kvcache pods one at a time. Also bump file descriptor limits on those nodes via sysctl if that's the cause. Luca, can you apply sysctl bump and coordinate with infra?
Luca (platform): applying sysctl changes to node pool now (`fs.file-max` and systemd limits). I'll cordon and drain one node at a time for safe restart.
Jon SRE: restarting kvcache pod kvcache-3 -> pod recycled, cache warmup in progress. Observability: 5xx rate dropping to 9.5% (5m).
Kevin (englead): good. Keep watching. If 5xx < 5% for 2 consecutive windows, we can de-escalate.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Acknowledgement recorded by Tina (oncall).
Tina (oncall): update customers: mitigation in progress, traffic diversion + node fixes applied. Monitoring shows error-rate falling. ETA 20m for full recovery.
Ashley (support): customer follow-ups: several enterprise customers asked for packet-level indicators — I asked PM for incident liaison and logged request.
Jon SRE: 5xx rate now 3.2% and trending down. Latency stabilizing. No new spikes in the last 4m.
Kevin (englead): confirming: region impacted = us-west1, root cause likely node-level FD/socket exhaustion causing backend kvcache failures. Action items: (1) platform apply permanent FD limit config, (2) add pod-level backpressure limits to routing proxy, (3) add alert for socket backlog.
Tina (oncall): I will hand off to next oncall in 30m if stable. For now leaving page un-closed until PD auto-resolves once 2 windows are ok.
incident-bot: :information_source: PD note: incident status changed -> monitoring.
Ashley (support): filing customer impact summary for postmortem: "Intermittent 502/504 in us-west1 affecting ~12% of requests for 25 minutes; top downstream impact on background batch customers; no data loss; mitigation by node restarts and traffic diversion."
Luca (platform): I'll open infra PR for fs/file-max + systemd limit changes and add rollout plan.
Jon SRE: leaving watch for 20m then will drop to low priority.
Tina (oncall): thanks team. tagging for postmortem: @Kevin (englead) @Jon SRE @Luca (platform) @Ashley (support).
Kevin (englead): noted. I'll draft RCA once PRs are in.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Monitoring OK — 5xx rate < 2% for 2 windows. PagerDuty auto-resolve scheduled in 10m.
Tina (oncall): handing off to Alex on next shift at 10:00UTC. I'll post final summary shortly.
Ashley (support): adding final customer note and linking PD incident.
Tina (oncall): final summary: root cause suspected: node-level socket/FD exhaustion in us-west1 hitting kvcache backends -> 502/504 surge; mitigation: scale proxies, divert traffic, restart kvcache pods, apply kernel limits; impact window ~09:12-09:38UTC. Moving to follow-up actions.
Kevin (englead): thanks. closing watch.
